label: copy step 1 with fed-back first token r, short sequences (L<=4)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase at the step right after the first copied output (recall_idx 1, t = L+1), when the fed-back input is r (i.e. the sequence starts with r). Strongly limited to short sequences: L=3 and L=4 fire about 1/2 to all of the time, L=5 fires only weakly and rarely, L>=6 never. Magnitude is highest for L=4 (t=5) and drops as more digits appear in the sequence. It does not fire on r in the original phase, on r at other copy positions, or on other first tokens (a handful of weak activations on p/y/f).

issues: The magnitude claim is wrong. The explanation says magnitude peaks at L=4 (t=5), but per-activation magnitude is about twice as high at L=3. Dev profile: L=3 has 472 active steps holding 0.321 of the activation mass (~6.8e-4 per step), and L=4 has 2241 active steps holding 0.665 (~3.0e-4 per step). L=4 only has the most total mass because it has more sequences.

The firing rate is understated. The explanation says 'about half or more' of r-first steps fire at L=3/4. Dev precision is 1.00 at L=3 (439/439) and 0.95 at L=4 (n_pred 2352), so the feature fires almost every time.

There is a systematic miss class at L=5. Overall, r-first L=5 sequences fire only 6.5% of the time (precision 0.065). When orig(1) is also r (sequences starting 'r r ...'), precision rises to 0.77 (111 predicted). These account for about half of the 178 L=5 activations, and the explanation does not mention them. Misses on the test split also show 'r r j y f' and 'r r b p t' at step 6.
The digit claim is weakly supported. At L=4, precision is 0.957 with 0 digits and 0.898 with >=2 digits. That shows only a small effect on whether the feature fires.

The main predicate holds up. Test P 0.970, R 0.936, F1 0.953, mass recall 0.987. Activity is only in the copy phase and only at recall_idx 1, and 99.8% of mass is on in_tok r. The remaining misses carry 1.3% of mass.
